c: A US president announces that Panama's General Noriega is in American custody.
INXS and Michael Hutchence tour the world with the album 'X' and 'Suicide Blonde'.
The Hubble Space Telescope is released into orbit, and then found to have a flawed mirror.
Madonna's Blond Ambition tour (cone bra and all) plays the world, and 'Vogue' tops the charts.
h: The very start of the decade.
e: 1990: Noriega captured (Jan), Hubble launched (Apr), INXS's 'X' tour, and Madonna's Blond Ambition tour. Mandela was also freed (Feb) and Germany reunified (Oct).

c: A US president addresses the nation as the ground war to free Kuwait begins.
David Campese stars as the Wallabies win the Rugby World Cup at Twickenham.
This NeXT computer at CERN runs the world's first website, which opens to the public.
Queen frontman Freddie Mercury dies, a day after revealing he has AIDS.
h: The Soviet Union doesn't make it to the end of this year.
e: 1991: the Desert Storm ground war (Feb), the Web went public (Aug), the Wallabies won the Rugby World Cup (Nov), Freddie Mercury died (Nov). Pinatubo erupted and the USSR dissolved.

c: George Bush, Bill Clinton and Ross Perot face off in a three-way presidential debate.
Australia and New Zealand host the Cricket World Cup; Imran Khan's Pakistan win the final at the MCG.
Space Shuttle Endeavour flies for the first time, and astronauts grab a stranded satellite by hand.
Euro Disney opens its gates outside Paris.
h: Barcelona hosts the Olympics and the 'Dream Team'.
e: 1992: the Cricket World Cup in Australia & NZ (Feb–Mar), Euro Disney opened (Apr), Endeavour's first flight (May), the Bush–Clinton–Perot debates (Oct). Hurricane Andrew hit Florida (Aug).

c: The FBI's 51-day siege of the Branch Davidian compound in Waco, Texas ends in fire. Listen to the agents' radio.
Shane Warne bowls Mike Gatting with the 'Ball of the Century' in his first Ashes Test.
Intel launches its very first Pentium processor.
Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You' from The Bodyguard is the biggest song of the year.
h: Bill Clinton's first year in the White House.
e: 1993: Pentium launched (Mar), the Waco siege ended (Apr), Warne's 'Ball of the Century' (Jun), and 'I Will Always Love You' ruled the charts. Also the Oslo Accords handshake and Sydney winning the 2000 Olympics.

c: Clinton, Yeltsin and Ukraine's Kravchuk sign a deal for Ukraine to give up its nuclear weapons.
Bushfires sweep through Sydney's suburbs and the Blue Mountains in January.
Sony launches its very first PlayStation in Japan.
Woodstock returns for its 25th anniversary, mud and all.
h: The Channel Tunnel opens between England and France.
e: 1994: the Ukraine nuclear deal (Jan), Sydney's bushfires (Jan), Woodstock '94 (Aug), PlayStation launched (Dec). Mandela also became president.

c: A US president speaks to the nation after the Oklahoma City bombing.
Newcastle teenagers Silverchair storm the charts with 'Tomorrow' and the album 'Frogstomp'.
Microsoft launches a new Windows with a brand-new 'Start' button.
Friends is TV's hottest show, and 'The Rachel' haircut is everywhere.
h: Toy Story becomes the first fully computer-animated feature film.
e: 1995: the Oklahoma City bombing (Apr), Silverchair's 'Frogstomp' (Mar), Windows 95 (Aug), Friends mania. Also eBay was founded.

c: Dolly the sheep is born, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
After the Port Arthur massacre in Tasmania, Australia hands in its guns in a famous buyback.
NASA launches Mars Pathfinder, carrying a tiny rover.
The whole world dances the Macarena.
h: Atlanta hosts the Olympic Games.
e: 1996: the Port Arthur massacre (Apr), Dolly the sheep born (Jul), the Macarena craze, Mars Pathfinder launched (Dec). Deep Blue also beat Kasparov in a game.

c: Israel's newly elected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visits the White House.
Australia's swimmers head to the Olympics, where Kieren Perkins wins the 1500m from lane eight.
The Nintendo 64 launches with Super Mario 64.
The Spice Girls tell you what they want, what they really really want.
h: England hosts Euro 96: 'football's coming home'.
e: 1996: Wannabe (Jul), Netanyahu's White House visit (Jul), Kieren Perkins' lane-eight gold in Atlanta (Jul), Nintendo 64 (Jun).

c: Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair hosts a US president after a Labour landslide.
A landslide at Thredbo ski village kills 18; Stuart Diver is pulled out alive.
The Sojourner rover becomes the first wheeled vehicle on Mars.
James Cameron's Titanic sails into cinemas and becomes the biggest film ever.
h: Hong Kong is handed back to China.
e: 1997: Blair's landslide (May), the Thredbo landslide (Jul), Pathfinder on Mars (Jul), Titanic released (Dec). Also the Hong Kong handover and Diana's death.

c: World leaders gather for the G8 summit in Birmingham, England.
A savage storm hits the Sydney to Hobart yacht race; six sailors die.
Two Stanford students found a search engine called Google.
Titanic wins 11 Oscars and Celine Dion's 'My Heart Will Go On' is everywhere.
h: France win the football World Cup on home soil.
e: 1998: Titanic's 11 Oscars (Mar), the Birmingham G8 (May), Google founded (Sep), the Sydney to Hobart tragedy (Dec).

c: NATO bombs Yugoslavia over Kosovo, and a US president explains why.
Steve Waugh's Australians win the Cricket World Cup at Lord's.
Governments and companies race to fix the 'Y2K bug' before midnight on New Year's Eve.
'...Baby One More Time' makes Britney Spears a superstar.
h: The last year before the 'millennium bug' was due to strike.
e: 1999: NATO's Kosovo campaign (Mar), Britney's breakthrough, Australia won the Cricket World Cup (Jun), the European eclipse (Aug), Y2K preparations. Putin became acting president on 31 December.

c: Russia's new president faces tough questions after the Kursk submarine sinks.
Cathy Freeman wins 400m gold in front of a home crowd.
The first crew moves into the International Space Station.
Russell Crowe's Gladiator is a box-office smash.
h: The Olympics come to Australia.
e: 2000: Gladiator (May), the Kursk disaster (Aug), Cathy Freeman's gold in Sydney (Sep), the first ISS crew (Nov).

c: A US president comments on an election too close to call: Bush v Gore.
The Olympic Games open with a spectacular ceremony at Stadium Australia.
Sony's PlayStation 2 launches and doubles as a DVD player.
Dr. Dre, Eminem and Snoop Dogg tour America on the Up in Smoke Tour.
h: The first year starting with a 2.
e: 2000: Kylie's 'Spinning Around' (Jun), the Concorde crash (Jul), the Up in Smoke Tour, the Sydney Olympics (Sep), PlayStation 2, and Bush v Gore (Nov).

c: A US president addresses the nation on the evening of the September 11 attacks.
Nicole Kidman stars in Baz Luhrmann's Moulin Rouge!
Dennis Tito pays $20 million to become the first space tourist.
Kylie Minogue's 'Can't Get You Out of My Head' tops the charts around the world.
h: The first year of the 21st century, strictly speaking.
e: 2001: Dennis Tito's space trip (Apr), Moulin Rouge! (May), Can't Get You Out of My Head (Sep), 9/11 (Sep). The first iPod also arrived.

c: Concorde and the Red Arrows fly over London for the Queen's Golden Jubilee.
Bombings at Bali nightclubs kill 202 people, including 88 Australians.
Spacewalking astronauts give Hubble a new camera and new solar wings.
Avril Lavigne becomes a 'Sk8er Boi' superstar with 'Complicated'.
h: Brazil win the World Cup in Japan and South Korea.
e: 2002: euro notes & coins arrived (Jan), Hubble's servicing mission (Mar), the Golden Jubilee (Jun), Avril Lavigne's breakthrough, the Bali bombings (Oct).

c: A statue of Saddam Hussein is pulled down in Baghdad.
A firestorm tears into Canberra's suburbs, destroying nearly 500 homes.
The Space Shuttle Columbia crew speak from orbit, days before the shuttle breaks up on re-entry.
The Return of the King premieres. It will win 11 Oscars.
h: Concorde makes its final commercial flight.
e: 2003: the Canberra firestorm (Jan), Columbia lost (Feb), Saddam's statue toppled (Apr), The Return of the King (Dec). Also Jonny Wilkinson's World Cup drop goal in Sydney.

c: A Boxing Day earthquake triggers a tsunami across the Indian Ocean.
Ian Thorpe, the 'Thorpedo', wins 200m and 400m freestyle gold in Athens.
Twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity land on Mars and send back these pictures.
Usher's 'Yeah!' is the biggest song of the year.
h: Athens hosts the Olympic Games.
e: 2004: Spirit & Opportunity on Mars (Jan), Usher's 'Yeah!', Thorpe's Athens golds (Aug), the Boxing Day tsunami (Dec). Facebook also launched.

c: Hurricane Katrina floods New Orleans and the Gulf Coast.
Riots break out on Cronulla Beach in Sydney's south.
NASA gets Discovery ready for the shuttle's 'Return to Flight' after the Columbia disaster.
Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith completes the prequel trilogy.
h: YouTube's very first video is uploaded.
e: 2005: Revenge of the Sith (May), Discovery's Return to Flight (Jul), Hurricane Katrina (Aug), the Cronulla riots (Dec).

c: Cardinal Ratzinger is elected Pope Benedict XVI.
The Socceroos beat Uruguay on penalties to reach their first World Cup in 32 years.
T-minus 10... an Atlas V launches the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.
Pink Floyd reunite at the Live 8 concert in Hyde Park.
h: Liverpool win the Champions League from 3–0 down in Istanbul.
e: 2005: Benedict XVI (Apr), Live 8 (Jul), the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter launch (Aug), the Socceroos reached the World Cup (Nov).

c: Venezuela's Hugo Chávez calls the US president 'the devil' at the UN: 'it still smells of sulphur'.
'Crocodile Hunter' Steve Irwin is killed by a stingray on the Great Barrier Reef.
Nintendo shows off the Wii, a console you control by waving a remote.
Daniel Craig makes his debut as James Bond in Casino Royale.
h: Pluto loses its status as a planet.
e: 2006: the Wii unveiled at E3 (May), Chávez at the UN (Sep), Steve Irwin's death (Sep), Casino Royale (Nov). Italy also won the World Cup.

c: Pakistan's Benazir Bhutto returns from exile, and is assassinated weeks later.
Sydney switches off its lights for the very first Earth Hour.
Space Shuttle Atlantis does a backflip before docking with the space station.
Fans queue at midnight for the final Harry Potter book.
h: Steve Jobs unveils a phone with no keyboard.
e: 2007: the iPhone unveiled (Jan), the first Earth Hour (Mar), Atlantis docked with the ISS (Jun), the last Harry Potter book (Jul), Bhutto assassinated (Dec).

c: Apache helicopters escort the Dutch team home from the Beijing Olympics.
Fans leave flowers for Australian actor Heath Ledger, who dies at 28.
The very first Android phone goes on sale.
The Dark Knight premieres, with Ledger's Joker set to win a posthumous Oscar.
h: Beijing hosts the Olympics and Usain Bolt runs 9.69.
e: 2008: Heath Ledger's death (Jan), The Dark Knight (Jul), the Beijing Olympics (Aug), the first Android phone (Sep), Lehman's collapse (Sep).

c: Crowds pour into the streets of Washington as Barack Obama is elected president.
Hundreds of thousands of pilgrims fill Sydney as the Pope arrives for World Youth Day.
The Large Hadron Collider is switched on under the Swiss–French border.
All four members of ABBA appear together at the Mamma Mia! movie premiere.
h: Michael Phelps wins eight gold medals at one Games.
e: 2008: Mamma Mia! (Jul), World Youth Day in Sydney (Jul), the LHC switched on (Sep), Obama elected (Nov).

c: A crowd fills the National Mall for a concert on the eve of a historic inauguration.
The Black Saturday bushfires kill 173 people in Victoria.
NASA launches Kepler to hunt for Earth-like planets.
The world says goodbye to Michael Jackson at a memorial in Los Angeles.
h: A plane lands safely on the Hudson River.
e: 2009: the 'We Are One' concert and Obama's inauguration (Jan), Black Saturday (Feb), Kepler launched (Mar), Michael Jackson died (Jun).

c: An Icelandic volcano's ash cloud grounds flights across Europe.
Mary MacKillop is declared Australia's first saint.
Apple unveils the iPad.
Christopher Nolan's Inception premieres.
h: 33 trapped Chilean miners are rescued.
e: 2010: the iPad (Jan), Eyjafjallajökull's ash cloud (Apr), Inception (Jul), Mary MacKillop canonised (Oct). Also the Burj Khalifa opened.

c: Rescuers scrub oil off birds after the Deepwater Horizon spill in the Gulf of Mexico.
16-year-old Jessica Watson sails into Sydney after sailing solo around the world.
The iPhone 4 arrives with FaceTime, and 'Antennagate'.
The droning vuvuzela becomes the sound of the World Cup in South Africa.
h: Spain win the World Cup for the first time.
e: 2010: Deepwater Horizon (Apr), Jessica Watson home (May), the iPhone 4 (Jun), vuvuzelas at the South Africa World Cup (Jun–Jul).

c: Tokyo shakes as a magnitude-9 earthquake hits Japan.
Floodwaters swamp Brisbane after weeks of record rain.
Apple fans leave tributes after Steve Jobs dies.
Adele's '21' and 'Someone Like You' rule the charts.
h: Prince William marries Kate Middleton.
e: 2011: the Brisbane floods (Jan), the Tōhoku earthquake & Fukushima (Mar), Adele's '21', Steve Jobs' death (Oct). Also the Arab Spring.

c: Osama bin Laden is killed in a US raid in Pakistan.
Category 5 Cyclone Yasi slams into north Queensland.
The final Space Shuttle mission lifts off.
The last Harry Potter film premieres in London's Trafalgar Square.
h: India win the Cricket World Cup at home.
e: 2011: Cyclone Yasi (Feb), bin Laden killed (May), the last shuttle launch (Jul), the final Harry Potter film (Jul).

c: The Olympic torch relay makes its way around Britain.
Gotye's 'Somebody That I Used to Know' hits No. 1 in America.
The $35 Raspberry Pi computer goes on sale.
Danny Boyle's opening ceremony features the Queen 'parachuting' in with James Bond.
h: London hosts the Olympics for a third time.
e: 2012: the Raspberry Pi (Feb), Gotye's US No. 1 (Apr), the torch relay and Olympic opening ceremony (Jul), Curiosity landed on Mars (Aug).

c: Hurricane Sandy batters the US East Coast.
Sally Pearson wins Olympic gold in the 100m hurdles.
Felix Baumgartner jumps from the edge of space and breaks the sound barrier.
'Gangnam Style' becomes the first YouTube video to reach a billion views.
h: The Queen celebrates her Diamond Jubilee.
e: 2012: Sally Pearson's gold (Aug), the Red Bull Stratos jump (Oct), Hurricane Sandy (Oct), Gangnam Style's billion views (Dec).

c: A meteor explodes over Chelyabinsk, Russia, injuring about 1,500 people.
Baz Luhrmann's The Great Gatsby, shot in Sydney, premieres.
Sony launches the PlayStation 4.
Beyoncé tours as 'Mrs Carter' and drops a surprise album overnight.
h: Andy Murray ends Britain's 77-year wait for a men's Wimbledon champion.
e: 2013: the Chelyabinsk meteor (Feb), Pope Francis (Mar), The Great Gatsby (May), the PS4 (Nov), Beyoncé's surprise album (Dec).

c: Edward Snowden, holed up in Moscow after leaking NSA secrets.
Vivid lights up the Sydney Opera House, which turns 40 this year.
Microsoft launches the Xbox One.
Miley Cyrus swings in on a 'Wrecking Ball'.
h: Prince George is born.
e: 2013: Vivid Sydney and the Opera House's 40th birthday, Snowden's leaks (Jun), Miley's 'Wrecking Ball' (Aug), the Xbox One (Nov). Also Typhoon Haiyan.

c: Germany beat Argentina in Rio to win the World Cup.
A gunman takes hostages at the Lindt Café in Sydney's Martin Place.
Rosetta reaches a comet and drops the Philae lander onto it.
Everyone is tipping ice water over their heads for the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge.
h: Brazil host the World Cup and lose 7–1 to Germany.
e: 2014: the World Cup in Brazil (Jun–Jul), the Ice Bucket Challenge (Aug), Philae lands on a comet (Nov), the Lindt Café siege (Dec).

c: World leaders gather in Paris to strike a deal on climate change.
Australia beat New Zealand at the MCG to win the Cricket World Cup.
New Horizons sends back the first close-up pictures of Pluto.
Star Wars: The Force Awakens premieres in Hollywood.
h: A spacecraft flies past Pluto for the first time.
e: 2015: Australia's Cricket World Cup (Mar), New Horizons at Pluto (Jul), The Force Awakens (Dec), the Paris climate agreement (Dec).

c: A US president phones the newly crowned Women's World Cup champions.
The Socceroos win the Asian Cup on home soil.
SpaceX lands an orbital rocket booster upright for the first time.
Hamilton opens on Broadway.
h: Cecil the lion is killed by a trophy hunter in Zimbabwe.
e: 2015: the Socceroos won the Asian Cup (Jan), Cecil the lion (Jul), Hamilton on Broadway (Aug), SpaceX's first booster landing (Dec).

c: The European Commission's president reacts as Britain votes to leave the EU.
The worst coral bleaching on record hits the Great Barrier Reef.
NASA's Juno spacecraft goes into orbit around Jupiter.
Fans leave flowers for David Bowie, who dies two days after releasing his last album.
h: Leicester City win the Premier League at 5000–1.
e: 2016: David Bowie's death (Jan), reef bleaching (Mar), the Brexit vote (Jun), Juno at Jupiter (Jul). Also Pokémon Go and the Rio Olympics.

c: A total solar eclipse crosses the entire United States.
Roger Federer beats Rafael Nadal in an epic Australian Open final in Melbourne.
Nintendo launches the Switch, a console you can take with you.
Wonder Woman becomes a box-office smash.
h: Cassini dives into Saturn to end its mission.
e: 2017: the Federer–Nadal Australian Open final (Jan), the Nintendo Switch (Mar), Wonder Woman (Jun), the Great American Eclipse (Aug).

c: France's youngest-ever president, Emmanuel Macron, makes his first trip abroad.
Cyclone Debbie batters Queensland's Whitsundays.
The fidget spinner becomes the must-have gadget in every school.
Ed Sheeran's 'Shape of You' is the biggest song of the year.
h: 'Despacito' becomes the most-watched video on YouTube.
e: 2017: Cyclone Debbie (Mar), Macron elected (May), the fidget-spinner craze, Ed Sheeran's 'Shape of You'.

c: Prince Harry marries Meghan Markle at Windsor.
Australian diving doctor Richard Harris helps rescue 12 boys and their coach from a flooded Thai cave.
Falcon Heavy blasts off carrying a Tesla Roadster, and its twin boosters land side by side.
Avengers: Infinity War ends with half the universe snapped away.
h: England reach a World Cup semi-final; France win it.
e: 2018: Falcon Heavy (Feb), Infinity War (Apr), Harry & Meghan's wedding (May), the Thai cave rescue (Jul).

c: Greta Thunberg leads millions of students on school strikes for the climate.
Ash Barty wins the French Open and becomes world No. 1.
Scientists reveal the first-ever picture of a black hole.
Avengers: Endgame becomes the highest-grossing film of all time.
h: Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris catches fire.
e: 2019: the Notre-Dame fire (Apr), the first black hole image (Apr), Endgame (Apr), Barty's French Open (Jun).

c: NATO's chief meets Britain's new Prime Minister, Boris Johnson.
Bushfire smoke smothers Canberra as the 'Black Summer' begins.
The first 5G phones go on sale.
Billie Eilish's 'Bad Guy' hits No. 1.
h: England win the Cricket World Cup on a super over.
e: 2019: the first 5G phones (Apr), Billie Eilish's 'Bad Guy', Boris Johnson became PM (Jul), the start of the Black Summer (Dec).

c: The world locks down as COVID-19 spreads.
Smoke from Australia's Black Summer bushfires can be seen from space.
SpaceX flies NASA astronauts to the space station, the first crewed launch from the US in nine years.
Fans mourn basketball legend Kobe Bryant after a helicopter crash.
h: 'You're on mute' becomes the phrase of the year.
e: 2020: the Black Summer bushfires (Jan), Kobe Bryant's death (Jan), COVID lockdowns (Mar), SpaceX's Demo-2 (May).

c: The giant Ever Given container ship gets stuck in the Suez Canal.
Melbourne becomes one of the most locked-down cities on Earth.
NASA's Perseverance rover lands on Mars.
Squid Game becomes Netflix's biggest show ever.
h: The 'Tokyo 2020' Olympics are held, a year late.
e: 2021: Perseverance landed (Feb), the Ever Given (Mar), Melbourne's lockdowns, Squid Game (Sep).

c: Rioters storm the US Capitol.
Ash Barty wins Wimbledon, 50 years after Evonne Goolagong's first title.
The Ingenuity helicopter makes the first powered flight on another planet. Listen to it hum on Mars!
Olivia Rodrigo's 'Drivers License' breaks streaming records.
h: The first all-civilian crew orbits the Earth.
e: 2021: the Capitol riot (Jan), Drivers License (Jan), Ingenuity's first flight (Apr), Barty's Wimbledon (Jul). Inspiration4 also flew.

c: Queen Elizabeth II dies after 70 years on the throne.
Shane Warne dies suddenly at 52, and fans flock to his statue at the MCG.
The James Webb Space Telescope releases its first pictures.
Top Gun: Maverick flies past a billion dollars at the box office.
h: Lionel Messi finally wins the World Cup.
e: 2022: Shane Warne's death (Mar), Top Gun: Maverick (May), Webb's first images (Jul), the Queen's death (Sep).

c: Elon Musk buys Twitter for $44 billion.
La Niña rains bring record floods to eastern Australia.
NASA's Artemis I sends an uncrewed Orion around the Moon.
Harry Styles' 'As It Was' is the biggest song of the year.
h: A chatbot called ChatGPT launches at the end of the year.
e: 2022: the eastern Australia floods, 'As It Was', Musk bought Twitter (Oct), Artemis I (Nov), ChatGPT (Nov).

c: Church bells ring out as King Charles III is crowned.
The Matildas reach the World Cup semi-finals; the nation stops for their penalty shootout.
India's Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole.
Barbie and Oppenheimer open on the same day: 'Barbenheimer'.
h: The Titan submersible is lost on a dive to the Titanic.
e: 2023: the coronation (May), Barbenheimer (Jul), the Matildas' World Cup run (Aug), Chandrayaan-3 (Aug).

c: Earthquakes devastate Turkey and Syria; rescuers pull survivors from the rubble.
Sydney hosts WorldPride, the first in the southern hemisphere.
ChatGPT sets off a worldwide AI boom.
Taylor Swift's Eras Tour becomes the first tour to earn a billion dollars.
h: King Charles III is crowned.
e: 2023: the Turkey–Syria earthquakes (Feb), Sydney WorldPride (Feb–Mar), the AI boom, the Eras Tour's billion dollars.

c: A total solar eclipse crosses North America.
Australia wins a record 18 gold medals at the Olympics.
SpaceX catches a Starship booster with giant 'chopsticks'.
The Paris Olympics open with a parade of boats along the Seine.
h: A cargo ship knocks down Baltimore's Key Bridge.
e: 2024: the North American eclipse (Apr), the Paris Olympics (Jul–Aug), Australia's 18 golds, Starship's booster catch (Oct).

c: Robert Prevost becomes Pope Leo XIV, the first American pope.
Cyclone Alfred bears down on Brisbane and floods northern NSW.
China's DeepSeek AI app stuns Silicon Valley.
Oasis reunite for their first tour in 16 years.
h: Thieves steal crown jewels from the Louvre in broad daylight.
e: 2025: DeepSeek (Jan), Cyclone Alfred (Mar), Pope Leo XIV (May), the Oasis reunion tour. Also Trump's second inauguration (Jan).

c: Firefighting 'Super Scooper' planes battle the Palisades fire in Los Angeles.
Oscar Piastri leads the Formula 1 championship for much of the season.
A NASA orbiter photographs Firefly's Blue Ghost, the first private lander to touch down upright on the Moon.
Arne Slot's Liverpool win the Premier League in his first season.
h: Nintendo releases the Switch 2.
e: 2025: the LA wildfires (Jan), Blue Ghost on the Moon (Mar), Liverpool champions (Apr), the Switch 2 (Jun), Piastri's title fight. Also the Louvre jewel heist (Oct).

c: Mexico City parties after a win at the first 48-team World Cup.
Australia hosts the Women's Asian Cup.
Artemis II flies four astronauts around the Moon, the first crewed lunar trip in over 50 years.
Bad Bunny headlines the Super Bowl halftime show.
h: Milan and Cortina host the Winter Olympics.
e: 2026: Bad Bunny's halftime show (Feb), the Women's Asian Cup in Australia (Mar), Artemis II (Apr), the 48-team World Cup (Jun–Jul), America's 250th (Jul).
